findings.source_quote: Examples: 'you' and plural/formal forms vary in the English source (general second-person usage)
findings.suggested_fix: Use a consistent Portuguese second-person register throughout the translation. Choose either the plural/formal 'vós'/ 'vossos' or the modern singular 'tu'/'teu' or the polite 'você'/'seu' and update all instances to match. For example, change instances of 'Se estás com o coração...' to 'Se estais com o coração...' (if adopting vós/estais) or change 'Confessai as vossas culpas uns aos outros' to 'Confessa as tuas culpas...' (if adopting tu) or to 'Confesse as suas culpas uns aos outros' (if adopting você). Keep Biblical-quotation plurals (e.g., older-style 'vossas') consistent with the chosen register.
findings.translation_quote: Examples in translation: uses 'vós' in Tiago quote and Hebrews quote ('Confessai as vossas culpas uns aos outros'; 'para que sareis'; 'Temamos, pois, ... ficando‑nos'), but later uses singular/informal 'tu'/'teu' ('Se estás com o coração...','teu trauma','podes ser curados','Credes?')
